images.title: The mean is the balance point
images.purpose: Shows that the mean 12 of 10, 10, 11 and 17 balances the distances on its two sides.
images.composition: One large horizontal number line across the middle of the frame, dots stacked above it, a balance triangle under the mean, and one bracket on each side of the mean. Plain white background, lots of empty space around the main object, no scenery, no people, no extra text.
images.exact_structure: A number line from 9 to 18 with 10 evenly spaced short ticks, one at every whole number. Numerals appear only under the ticks at 10, 11 and 17; all other ticks have no numerals. Four teal (#0072B2) dots sit above the line: two stacked at 10, one at 11, one at 17. A large reddish purple (#CC79A7) filled triangle points up at 12 from just below the line, with the label 'mean 12' under it. A thin grey bracket above the dots spans from 10 to 12 with the label 'left total 5' above it; a second thin grey bracket spans from 12 to 17 with the label 'right total 5' above it. The two brackets are drawn at the same height. Exactly 4 dots, 1 triangle, 2 brackets.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
images.takeaway: The distances on the left of the mean add up to the same total as those on the right.
images.description: Shows that the mean 12 of 10, 10, 11 and 17 balances the distances on its two sides.
images.teaching_notes: Midpoint of the extremes would be 13.5, not the mean; the picture shows only the true centre.

image_decisions.why: The balance picture is the core of this concept: the mean is where the left and right distances match.
